title: Family needs Emotional needs
status: draft: written 19 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 3 Environmental Activities; not yet checked by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Children are never asked to say whose home lacks love. A child who says no one at home cares for him or her, or who shows fear of an adult, is listened to privately and the school safeguarding policy followed.

skills.key_step: The child names a feeling from a face, the body and the story (happy, sad, angry, afraid, surprised) and says how people show it.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the basic needs of a family.
floor.question: Name one basic need of a family.

steps: Make a feeling face in the mirror.
Look at eyes and body as well as the mouth.
Tell what made the person feel that way.
contexts: a child left out of a game

board.do: Draw a child with wide eyes and raised hands.
Point at the eyes and hands.
Wait for the child to look at the whole body and answer.
Write the feeling word under the face: afraid.

misconceptions.ask: Otieno falls and cries. What is he feeling?
misconceptions.repair: Read a story where a father cries at good news. Say: everyone has feelings, boys and girls.

misconceptions.ask: Grandmother cries when her son comes home after many years. How does she feel?
misconceptions.repair: Show a picture of a happy reunion with tears. Ask what made her cry, then name joy.

listen_for: Yes, she is angry so she is bad
misconceptions.ask: Achieng feels angry when her book is torn. Is Achieng a bad girl?
misconceptions.repair: Separate the feeling from the action: angry is fine, hitting is not. Practise calm steps: breathe, tell an adult.

misconceptions.ask: A child stands shaking with wide eyes and an open mouth while a dog barks. How does she feel?
misconceptions.repair: Look at eyes, hands and body as well as the mouth. Act out afraid with the whole body.

checks.question: A girl smiles and jumps up and down. How does she feel?

skills.key_step: The child names emotional needs (love, care, comfort, praise, being listened to, safety) and says how each is met in real life.

floor.question: A child cries because her pet died. How does she feel?

representations: a needs chart with a new column for love and care
steps: Name the feeling in the story.
Act out how to meet the need.
Say why gifts alone do not meet it.
contexts: a new child at school with no friends
a child whose drawing is good

board.do: Draw a child sitting alone at break time.
Wait for the child to say a friend, someone to play with or talk to.

misconceptions.ask: Baraka is sad because his grandfather is sick. What will help him most?
misconceptions.repair: Role-play two ways to help a sad friend: a sweet and walking away, or listening. Ask which felt better.

listen_for: No, only food, clothes and a house are needs
misconceptions.repair: Add a fourth column to the needs chart: love, care, praise. Say: we need these to grow well inside.

listen_for: Nothing, adults do not need comfort
misconceptions.ask: Mother is tired and sad after a long day. What can a child do?
misconceptions.repair: Tell a story of a child who comforts a parent. Everyone needs love, at every age.

misconceptions.ask: Akinyi sweeps the class well. What should the teacher say?
misconceptions.repair: Show how praise makes a classmate want to help again. Praise the action, kindly.

checks.question: A new pupil has no friends. What does she need?
checks.answer: Someone to play with and welcome her

checks.question: Is praise a way of meeting an emotional need?
